sources.title: Nez Perce Tribe: History
sources.note: Direct tribal account, Traditional Ways and Treaties. Homeland, specialist leaders/councils, sovereignty and allotment. Reservation acreage differs from NPS wording, so numerical acreage omitted.

sources.title: National Park Service: Nez Perce Village
sources.note: Direct paragraphs on river benches, salmon, canoes, horse arrival and trade. No exact archaeological continuity date inferred from location alone.

sources.title: National Park Service: Camas
sources.note: Direct Pivotal Places article: small bulbs retained, September 1805 family processing, earthen kilns, Gass comparison and ecological knowledge. No medical or foraging instructions.

sources.title: National Park Service: Freshwater Plants
sources.note: Direct tule mat material behavior, household uses, portability and sedge cordage paragraphs.

sources.title: National Park Service museum: Cradleboard, NEPE 57
sources.note: Original indexed museum label, circa 1900, wood/buckskin with velveteen hood and female relatives carrying children. Medical/developmental benefits claimed in label are not repeated.

sources.title: Ellie Kaplan, National Park Service: Ida Blackeagle
sources.note: Direct biography, learned at twelve, Lapwai school teaching, 1966 hiring with Viola Morris, cornhusk adaptation after restricted mobility.

sources.title: National Park Service: The Treaty Period
sources.note: Direct 1855/1863 chronology, 1860 gold discovery, refusal of outside bands and Senate ratification in 1867. Conflicting acreage omitted.

sources.title: National Park Service: The Flight of 1877
sources.note: Direct park account, non-treaty bands, 126-day flight exceeding 1,170 miles; Big Hole and Bear Paw dates. Not all Nez Perce participated.

sources.title: National Park Service: Aftermath of the Flight of 1877
sources.note: Direct Living in Exile, Escape to Canada, Today sections. 1885 return to Northwest, dispersed communities and Joseph not returned to Wallowa. No historic oral testimony quoted.

sources.title: Nez Perce Tribe: Niimiipuu Language Program
sources.note: Direct Words and Phrases, Hunting table: exact ’íin ’eekíce poxpok’láana / I see a ball. Opening explains Elders-approved spelling and lowercase convention; modern teaching witness.

sources.title: Columbia River Inter-Tribal Fish Commission: Welcoming back the Little Salmon, 2013
sources.note: Direct tribal commission report quoting project staff: 1994 eggs saved from disposal, reintroduction and sovereignty. First-release figure differs from later federal summary, so that quantity is omitted.

sources.title: National Park Service, Mesa Verde: The Ute People
sources.note: Direct Ute subsection distinguishes seasonal mountain homelands and three contemporary tribes. Ancestral Pueblo buildings at Mesa Verde are not attributed to Ute builders.

sources.title: Southern Ute Indian Tribe: History
sources.note: Direct selected household passages only: winter stories/repairs, yucca soap, pitch-sealed baskets and Academy opening. Page has problematic broad linguistic/Spanish chronology and medical efficacy claims, none adopted.

sources.title: Sam Burns and Liesl Dees, Fort Lewis College: Ute relationships to the lands of West Central Colorado, 2004
sources.note: Direct US Forest Service/NPS-supported ethnographic study, Parts I and II. Contemporary Ute elder interviews plus historical synthesis. Used for family mobility, changing political labels, trading post and 1881 removal; not universalized to all Ute practice.

sources.title: Dominguez Archaeological Research Group: Colorado Wickiup Project
sources.note: Original indexed investigators’ project report/abstracts. Volume III records twelve sites in 2005-2006 and 81 wooden structures/features, including low platforms, storage shelf and utility poles. Broader project distinguishes Ute and other Numic attribution.

sources.title: History Colorado: Miniature moccasins, object 02009.117.97.A
sources.note: Direct access failed; original indexed museum record states 16 March 2015 review with designated representatives of three Ute tribes identified likely doll use; provenance Dragon, Utah, Flavey family 1907-1923. No photograph inspected and no exact manufacture date inferred.

sources.title: Damon Toledo, The Southern Ute Drum: History of the Bear Dance, 2015
sources.note: Direct interviews with Matthew J. Box and Tara Vigil; modern Memorial Day scheduling, clothing workshops, aunt teaching feast organization and final-day stew. Opening claim oldest/fifteenth-century dance not adopted.

sources.title: Oklahoma State University, Indian Affairs: Brunot Agreement, 1873
sources.note: Direct original text, entered Los Pinos 13 September 1873 and ratified 29 April 1874; Article I land cession, II hunting, III annual trust, V continued protections. Erroneous Makah metadata tag not used.

sources.title: Ute Mountain Ute Tribe: Cultural/Language Program
sources.note: Direct opening program list: Head Start/toddlers, adult language, beadwork/cradleboard/moccasin classes and fourth-grade curriculum collaboration. Resources directly links dictionary. Template filler and undated scheduling claims omitted.

sources.title: Ute Mountain Ute Dictionary: Morphology guide
sources.note: Direct Silent Vowel Alternations table: Kaan akagar. / This house is red. Page introduction identifies Southern Ute grammar; resource endorsed by official Ute Mountain language-program link. Modern teaching, not precontact inscription.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Share same people-level narrative, preserving distinct imported dates. Tribal History and Language pages identify Nimiipuu/Nez Perce; both decoded polygons cover adjoining inland Northwest areas, not an Oklahoma reservation or different nation.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Share broad Ute people narrative only. Both decoded outlines span Utah/Colorado, with the 1492 footprint somewhat broader; no distinct later reservation is being retrojected. Public text treats these as approximate regions and distinguishes three present-day tribes. Imported endonym spelling is not reused as a verified language specimen.
